name: Open-Ended Text Response
summary: Learners type free-form text in response to a prompt; Pimpi evaluates the response in character against a rubric and gives warm, specific feedback.

aiGenerability.notes: AI generates prompts and rubrics easily. Pimpi evaluates the response in character against the rubric — works best with concrete, checkable criteria ('mentions at least 2 causes', 'uses evidence from the text'). Subjective criteria ('is the writing eloquent?') are harder to evaluate reliably. Pimpi's feedback is warm and conversational, never shows numeric scores to the kid.

prompt.description: The open-ended question or prompt. e.g., 'In your own words, explain why the dinosaurs went extinct' or 'Describe a time you solved a problem.'

modelAnswer.description: A high-quality sample answer for reference and learning. Shown to learner after submission or in feedback.

rubric.description: Scoring rubric for AI or manual evaluation.

criterion.description: The skill or concept being assessed. e.g., 'Mentions at least 2 causes', 'Uses evidence from the text', 'Clear explanations'.

maxPoints.description: Maximum points for this criterion. e.g., 5, 10.

exemplar.description: Example text that meets this criterion, for AI evaluation training.

maxLength.description: Maximum character count. Ages 8-10: 200. Ages 11-13: 500. Ages 14-16: 1000.

explanation.description: Context or guidance for human reviewers when grading.

pimpiEvalPrompt.description: System prompt for Pimpi when evaluating the kid's response. Includes the rubric criteria, the model answer for reference, topic context, and Pimpi's personality rules. Generated by the Spark generator, not hand-written. See the Pimpi Evaluator section in the mechanic description.

ux.mobileNotes: Use a large text area (minimum 200px height). Show a character counter (e.g., '47 / 500 characters'). On mobile, ensure the keyboard doesn't cover the text area (pan or expand). Auto-save drafts to prevent data loss. Placeholder text should hint at desired response length and type.

ageAdaptations.8-10: Simple, concrete prompts requiring 1-2 sentence responses. Max 200 characters. Prompt framing is supportive ('Tell me about...', 'Draw a picture with words...'). Rubric is simple (1-2 criteria, max 10 points total). Example: 'Describe your favorite animal in 1-2 sentences.' Model answer shows 1-2 clear sentences.
ageAdaptations.11-13: Paragraph-length prompts requiring inference or synthesis. Max 500 characters (roughly 75-100 words). Rubric has 2-3 criteria (clarity, evidence, completeness). Example: 'Explain why the American Revolution happened. Give at least 2 reasons.' Model answer shows a paragraph with multiple reasons and brief explanations.
ageAdaptations.14-16: Analytical or argumentative prompts. Max 1000 characters. Rubric has 3-4 criteria (thesis clarity, evidence quality, reasoning, organization). Example: 'Analyze the symbolism in [work]. What does the [symbol] represent and why does it matter?' Model answer demonstrates sophisticated analysis, nuanced interpretation, and clear evidence use.
